steps: Identify which calculation: gas volume, atom economy, or percentage yield
For a gas volume: find moles of the gas from the equation, then multiply by 24
For atom economy: Mr of desired product ÷ Mr of ALL products × 100
For yield: actual ÷ theoretical × 100, and state the unit
method_card.title: Gas Volumes and Atom Economy
method_card.content:
Three calculations, three different questions.

Gas volume at RTP: one mole of any gas fills 24 dm³. Multiply moles by 24 for the volume, or divide by 24 to get moles.

Atom economy is about the equation: the fraction of the product mass that is the substance you want, \(\frac{M_r\text{ desired}}{M_r\text{ all products}} \times 100\). Multiply each product's Mr by its coefficient first.

Percentage yield is about the experiment: \(\frac{\text{actual}}{\text{theoretical}} \times 100\), always below 100%.

Check whether your board gives you the molar volume or expects you to recall it.

exam_context.frequency: High: atom economy and gas volumes are common higher chemistry calculations

gold.display: 3.25 g of zinc reacts with excess HCl: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂. The student collects 960 cm³ of hydrogen at RTP. Calculate the percentage yield. (Ar: Zn = 65)

misconceptions.message: Moles Zn = 3.25/65 = 0.05. Ratio 1:1, so moles H₂ = 0.05. Theoretical volume = 0.05 × 24 = 1.2 dm³ = 1200 cm³. Yield = (960/1200) × 100 = 80%.
Convert to the same units. 960 cm³ and 1200 cm³, or 0.96 dm³ and 1.2 dm³.

gold.hint: Theoretical volume in cm³ first, then actual over theoretical times 100.

guided_steps.say: A yield with a gas: find the theoretical volume, match the units, then compare. Ratio Zn : H₂ is 1 : 1.

guided_steps.hint: Divide the mass by the Ar.

guided_steps.pre: Ratio 1 : 1, so theoretical moles of H₂ =
The collected gas is in cm³, so convert: 1.2 × 1000 =

guided_steps.done: That equals the 960 cm³ collected, so 80% is right.

misconceptions.message: Route B: Mr of all products = 56 + 18 = 74. AE = (56/74) × 100 = 75.7%. Route A would be 56%.
Use Mr of all products (56 + 18 = 74), not Mr of reactant.

gold.hint: Add both Route B product Mr, then desired over total times 100.

guided_steps.say: Route B only. The products are CaO and H₂O.

guided_steps.hint: Add the two product Mr values.

guided_steps.pre: The desired product CaO has Mr =
Check: waste H₂O is about 24.3%. Useful plus waste = 75.7 + 24.3 =
guided_steps.done: They total 100%, so Route B is 75.7%.

gold.display: 32 g of iron(III) oxide reacts with carbon monoxide: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂. Calculate the volume of CO₂ produced at RTP. (Mr: Fe₂O₃ = 160)

misconceptions.message: Moles Fe₂O₃ = 32/160 = 0.2. From equation: 1 Fe₂O₃ → 3 CO₂. Moles CO₂ = 0.2 × 3 = 0.6. Volume = 0.6 × 24 = 14.4 dm³.
1 mole of Fe₂O₃ produces 3 moles of CO₂. Multiply by 3.

gold.hint: Mass to moles, apply the 1:3 ratio, then times 24.

guided_steps.say: Mass to moles, then the 1 : 3 ratio to CO₂, then volume.

guided_steps.hint: Divide the mass by the Mr.

guided_steps.pre: Ratio 1 Fe₂O₃ : 3 CO₂, so moles of CO₂ = 0.2 × 3 =

guided_steps.done: Back to 0.6 mol of CO₂, so 14.4 dm³ is right.

gold.display: 12.25 g of potassium chlorate decomposes: 2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂. Calculate the volume of oxygen produced at RTP. (Ar: K = 39, Cl = 35.5, O = 16)

misconceptions.message: Mr KClO₃ = 39 + 35.5 + (3×16) = 122.5. Moles = 12.25/122.5 = 0.1. From equation: 2KClO₃ → 3O₂, so 0.1 mol → 0.15 mol O₂. Volume = 0.15 × 24 = 3.6 dm³.
The ratio is 2 : 3 (KClO₃ : O₂). 0.1 mol KClO₃ gives 0.1 × 3/2 = 0.15 mol O₂.

gold.hint: Find Mr, then moles, then the 2:3 ratio, then times 24.

guided_steps.say: Find Mr, then moles, then the 2 : 3 ratio, then volume.

guided_steps.hint: Add K, Cl and three O.
Divide the mass by the Mr.

guided_steps.done: Back to 0.15 mol of O₂, so 3.6 dm³ is right.

misconceptions.message: Moles CaCO₃ = 2.5/100 = 0.025. 1:1 ratio, moles CO₂ = 0.025. Theoretical volume = 0.025 × 24 = 0.6 dm³ = 600 cm³. Yield = (504/600) × 100 = 84%.
Convert: 504 cm³ and 600 cm³ (or 0.504 dm³ and 0.6 dm³).

gold.hint: Theoretical volume of CO₂ in cm³ first, then actual over theoretical times 100.

guided_steps.say: Theoretical volume of CO₂ first, then match units, then compare. Ratio CaCO₃ : CO₂ is 1 : 1.

guided_steps.hint: Divide the mass by the Mr.

guided_steps.pre: Ratio 1 : 1, so theoretical moles of CO₂ =

gold.display: In the decomposition 2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂, the desired product is oxygen. Calculate the atom economy. (Ar: K = 39, Cl = 35.5, O = 16)

misconceptions.message: Don't use Mr of reactants. Use Mr of ALL products: 2KCl + 3O₂ = 149 + 96 = 245.

gold.hint: Multiply each product Mr by its coefficient before adding.

guided_steps.say: The desired product is 3O₂. Use the coefficients on every product.

guided_steps.pre: Check: waste 2KCl is about 60.8%. Useful plus waste = 39.2 + 60.8 =
guided_steps.done: They total 100%, so 39.2% is right.

bronze.display: Calculate the volume occupied by 0.5 mol of hydrogen gas at RTP. Give your answer in dm³.

misconceptions.message: At RTP, 1 mole of any gas = 24 dm³. Volume = 0.5 × 24 = 12 dm³.

bronze.hint: Multiply the moles by 24, the molar volume at RTP.

guided_steps.say: At RTP, one mole of any gas fills 24 dm³, whatever the gas. \(V = \text{moles} \times 24\).

guided_steps.pre: Write the molar volume at RTP, in dm³:
guided_steps.hint: One mole of any gas fills this many dm³ at RTP.
Multiply the number of moles by 24.

guided_steps.done: Matches. Half a mole fills half of 24 dm³, so the volume is 12 dm³.

bronze.display: A gas has a volume of 4.8 dm³ at RTP. Calculate the number of moles of gas.

misconceptions.message: Moles = volume ÷ 24 = 4.8 ÷ 24 = 0.2 mol. Don't multiply.

bronze.hint: Divide the volume by 24 to get moles.

guided_steps.say: Turn the equation around: \(\text{moles} = \frac{V}{24}\).

guided_steps.pre: Write the molar volume at RTP, in dm³:
guided_steps.hint: Divide by this to go from volume to moles.

guided_steps.done: Back to 4.8 dm³, so 0.2 mol is right.

bronze.display: Calculate the volume of 2 mol of oxygen gas at RTP in dm³.

misconceptions.message: Volume = moles × 24 = 2 × 24 = 48 dm³.

guided_steps.say: At RTP, one mole of any gas fills 24 dm³. \(V = \text{moles} \times 24\).

bronze.display: In the reaction CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂, the only desired product is CaO. Calculate the atom economy. (Mr: CaO = 56, CO₂ = 44)
bronze.equation_hint: \(\text{atom economy} = \frac{M_r \text{ of desired product}}{M_r \text{ of all products}} \times 100\)

misconceptions.message: Use Mr of ALL products: 56 + 44 = 100. Atom economy = (56/100) × 100 = 56%. Don't use reactant Mr.

bronze.hint: Add both product Mr for the denominator, then divide the desired Mr and times 100.

guided_steps.say: Atom economy is the fraction of the product mass that is the bit you want. \(\text{AE} = \frac{M_r\text{ desired}}{M_r\text{ all products}} \times 100\).

guided_steps.pre: Add the Mr of all products: 56 + 44 =
The desired product (CaO) has Mr 56. Atom economy = (56 ÷ 100) × 100 =
guided_steps.hint: Divide 56 by the total, then times 100.

guided_steps.pre: Check: the waste CO₂ is 44 out of 100, so 44%. Useful plus waste: 56 + 44 =
guided_steps.hint: Add the useful percent and the waste percent.
guided_steps.done: They add to 100%, so an atom economy of 56% is right.

bronze.display: In the reaction 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO, the desired product is MgO. Calculate the atom economy.
bronze.equation_hint: \(\text{atom economy} = \frac{M_r \text{ of desired product}}{M_r \text{ of all products}} \times 100\)

misconceptions.message: There is only one product (MgO), so all atoms end up in the desired product. Atom economy = 100%.

bronze.hint: Only one product means every atom ends up in it.

guided_steps.say: Atom economy: \(\frac{M_r\text{ desired}}{M_r\text{ all products}} \times 100\). Count the products first.

guided_steps.pre: How many different products in 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO?
guided_steps.hint: Look to the right of the arrow.

Check: the waste is 0%, so useful = 100 − 0 =
guided_steps.done: No waste product, so the atom economy is 100%.

bronze.display: A student expected to make 10 g of a salt but only obtained 7.5 g. Calculate the percentage yield.

misconceptions.message: Percentage yield = (actual ÷ theoretical) × 100 = (7.5 ÷ 10) × 100 = 75%.

guided_steps.say: Percentage yield compares what you got to what you could have got. \(\%\text{ yield} = \frac{\text{actual}}{\text{theoretical}} \times 100\).

guided_steps.pre: Write the theoretical (expected) mass, in g:
guided_steps.hint: The mass you expected to make.
Divide actual by theoretical, then times 100.

guided_steps.done: That equals the 7.5 g actually made, so 75% is right.

bronze.display: In the reaction 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂, 0.1 mol of H₂O₂ decomposes. Calculate the volume of O₂ produced at RTP in dm³.

misconceptions.message: From the equation, 2 mol H₂O₂ → 1 mol O₂. So 0.1 mol H₂O₂ → 0.05 mol O₂. Volume = 0.05 × 24 = 1.2 dm³.

bronze.hint: Use the equation ratio to get moles of O₂ first, then times 24.

guided_steps.say: First the ratio, then the volume. From 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂, two moles of H₂O₂ make one mole of O₂.

guided_steps.pre: Moles of O₂ from 0.1 mol H₂O₂: 0.1 ÷ 2 =
guided_steps.hint: Two H₂O₂ make one O₂, so halve.
Multiply the moles of gas by 24.

guided_steps.done: Back to 0.05 mol of O₂, so 1.2 dm³ is right.

bronze.display: A gas occupies 7.2 dm³ at RTP. Calculate the number of moles of gas.

misconceptions.message: Moles = volume ÷ 24 = 7.2 ÷ 24 = 0.3 mol.
Divide by 24, don't multiply. Moles = 7.2 ÷ 24 = 0.3 mol.

guided_steps.say: Turn the equation around: \(\text{moles} = \frac{V}{24}\).

guided_steps.pre: Write the molar volume at RTP, in dm³:

guided_steps.done: Back to 7.2 dm³, so 0.3 mol is right.

misconceptions.message: Moles CaCO₃ = 5/100 = 0.05. Ratio 1:1, so moles CO₂ = 0.05. Volume = 0.05 × 24 = 1.2 dm³.

silver.hint: Mass to moles, then the 1:1 ratio, then times 24.

guided_steps.say: Three moves: mass to moles, ratio, then volume. \(n = \frac{\text{mass}}{M_r}\).

guided_steps.hint: Divide the mass by the Mr.

silver.display: 4.6 g of sodium reacts with water: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂. Calculate the volume of hydrogen gas produced at RTP in dm³. (Ar: Na = 23)

misconceptions.message: Moles Na = 4.6/23 = 0.2. From equation: 2Na → 1H₂, so moles H₂ = 0.2/2 = 0.1. Volume = 0.1 × 24 = 2.4 dm³.
2 moles of Na produce 1 mole of H₂. Halve the moles of Na.

silver.hint: Mass to moles, halve for the 2:1 ratio, then times 24.

guided_steps.say: Mass to moles, then halve for the ratio, then volume.

guided_steps.hint: Divide the mass by the Ar.
Two sodiums make one hydrogen molecule, so halve.
Multiply the moles of gas by 24.

guided_steps.done: Back to 0.1 mol of H₂, so 2.4 dm³ is right.

silver.display: 0.6 g of magnesium reacts with excess HCl: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. Calculate the volume of hydrogen produced at RTP in dm³. (Ar: Mg = 24)

misconceptions.message: Moles Mg = 0.6/24 = 0.025. Ratio 1:1 for Mg:H₂. Volume = 0.025 × 24 = 0.6 dm³.

silver.hint: Mass to moles, 1:1 ratio, then times 24.

guided_steps.say: Mass to moles, then volume. Ratio Mg : H₂ is 1 : 1.

guided_steps.hint: Divide the mass by the Ar.

guided_steps.done: Back to 0.025 mol, so 0.6 dm³ of H₂ is right.

silver.display: 10 g of iron(III) oxide is reduced: 2Fe₂O₃ + 3C → 4Fe + 3CO₂. The student obtains 5.6 g of iron. Calculate the percentage yield. (Mr: Fe₂O₃ = 160, Ar: Fe = 56)

misconceptions.message: Moles Fe₂O₃ = 10/160 = 0.0625. From equation: 2 mol Fe₂O₃ → 4 mol Fe, so 0.0625 → 0.125 mol Fe. Theoretical mass = 0.125 × 56 = 7.0 g. Yield = (5.6/7.0) × 100 = 80%.
The ratio is 2 Fe₂O₃ : 4 Fe, which simplifies to 1 : 2. Double the moles.

silver.hint: Find theoretical mass of Fe first, then actual over theoretical times 100.

guided_steps.say: Yield needs the theoretical mass first. Mass to moles, ratio, moles to mass, then compare.

guided_steps.hint: Divide the mass by the Mr.

guided_steps.pre: Ratio 2Fe₂O₃ : 4Fe is 1 : 2, so moles of Fe = 0.0625 × 2 =

guided_steps.done: That equals the 5.6 g obtained, so 80% is right.

silver.display: In the reaction Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂, the desired product is iron. Calculate the atom economy. (Mr: Fe = 56, CO₂ = 44)
silver.equation_hint: \(\text{atom economy} = \frac{M_r \text{ of desired}}{M_r \text{ of all products}} \times 100\)

guided_steps.say: Watch the coefficients. The desired product is 2Fe, and the products are 2Fe and 3CO₂.

guided_steps.pre: Check: waste 3CO₂ is about 54.1%. Useful plus waste = 45.9 + 54.1 =
guided_steps.hint: Add the useful and waste percentages.
guided_steps.done: They add to 100%, so 45.9% is right.

silver.equation_hint: \(\text{atom economy} = \frac{M_r \text{ of desired}}{M_r \text{ of all products}} \times 100\)

misconceptions.message: NH₃ is the only product. When there is only one product, atom economy = 100%.

silver.hint: Only one product, so atom economy is 100%.

guided_steps.say: Only one product here, so no atoms are wasted.

guided_steps.pre: How many different products in N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃?
guided_steps.hint: Look to the right of the arrow.

guided_steps.pre: Mr of the desired product NH₃ = 14 + (3 × 1) =
With only NH₃ as product, atom economy = (17 ÷ 17) × 100 =
guided_steps.hint: Desired over total; they are the same.

guided_steps.done: One product means 100% atom economy.

problem_bank.bronze_description: One equation, values already in the right units: molar volume (× or ÷ 24), a single atom economy, or a straight percentage yield.
problem_bank.silver_description: Two moves: convert mass to moles or apply a mole ratio first, then find the volume, yield or atom economy.
problem_bank.gold_description: Multi-step: chain mass, ratio, volume and a unit conversion, or work a yield or atom economy from a full balanced equation.

bronze.title: Bronze: one equation, straight in
steps: For a gas at RTP, one mole fills 24 dm³. Multiply moles by 24 for the volume; divide volume by 24 for the moles.
Atom economy = Mr of the product you want ÷ Mr of all products × 100. Percentage yield = actual ÷ theoretical × 100.
Always finish with the unit: dm³, mol, or %.

example.question: Calculate the volume of 0.25 mol of carbon dioxide at RTP, in dm³.

silver.title: Silver: convert first, then solve
steps: Turn grams into moles before anything else: \(n = \frac{\text{mass}}{M_r}\).
Then use the balanced equation's ratio to get the moles of the substance you actually want.
Finish the job: × 24 for a gas volume, or × Ar for a mass, then state the unit.

example.question: 4.0 g of calcium reacts fully with water: Ca + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + H₂. Find the volume of H₂ at RTP, in dm³. (Ar: Ca = 40)

gold.title: Gold: chain the whole method
steps: For yield: find the theoretical amount from the equation, match units (1 dm³ = 1000 cm³), then actual ÷ theoretical × 100.
For atom economy from a balanced equation, multiply every product's Mr by its coefficient before adding them up.
Keep each stage separate so one slip does not sink the rest.
